about: A four-second clip under a speed curve that rises in a straight line from normal speed at its start to three times at its end. Its average speed is two, so it lasts two seconds, and after t seconds it has played t + t²/2 seconds of its source: output frame k shows the source frame that holds that time, and the pips of source seconds 1, 2 and 3 are heard where the curve reaches them, at 0.732, 1.236 and 1.646 s, at their own pitch. A failure means a speed curve's length, its mapping of timeline time to source time, or its sound's place under the curve changed, or picture and sound follow different curves.

known.why: Under a curve the sound is laid in grains of 5.3 ms, each at the source position the curve gives its middle, and a pip's first grain starts sounding before the pip does: 1.1 ms early at 2.2 times speed and 1.5 ms at 2.7, where at twice a steady speed it is 0.9 ms. Grains that start on an onset rather than straddle it would end it.
